title: Finite scalar quotient and transition models for a supplied chain comparison
statement: Fix $\ell,E,L,\iota,g:X\simeq Y$, the completed rings $R_W,S_W$, finite coefficient rings $A_{W,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1}$, $B_{W,n}=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^{n+1}$, and all specified coefficient maps and model predicates of [lem-weil-isomorphism-scalar-completed-model]. No stalkwise invertibility assumption is needed here. Supply a natural chain isomorphism $b_P:G_EP\otimes_{R_X}S_X\simeq G_L(P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y)$ on good complexes with $b_P(c_L(s)\otimes x)=s\otimes x$. There exist natural finite comparisons $b_{P,n}:G_{E,n}(P\otimes_{R_Y}A_{Y,n})\otimes_{A_{X,n}}B_{X,n}\simeq G_{L,n}(P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{Y,n})$, quotient maps $v_n,w_n$ and adjacent transitions $t_n,u_n$, in the actual chosen cochain tensor models. Their local rules are $s\otimes(a\otimes x)\mapsto(c_{L,n}^{-1}(s)\iota_n(a))\otimes x$; $v_n(c_L(s)\otimes x)=\pi^L_{X,n}(c_L(s))\otimes(1\otimes x)$; $w_n(s\otimes x)=\pi^L_{Y,n}(s)\otimes x$; $t_n$ reduces both finite scalar factors and $u_n$ reduces its sole finite scalar factor. After restriction to $S_X$, the quotient square $b_P;w_n=v_n;b_{P,n}$ and transition square $b_{P,n+1};u_n=t_n;b_{P,n}$ commute. There is no derived comparison or preservation assertion in this statement.

proof.text: Form the two ScalarQuotientChain.Tower records from the completed coefficient rings, the finite coefficient rings, their actual projections, and their transitions. The identity completedCoefficientMap followed by a projection equals the E projection followed by integralScalarQuotientSheafMap; compatibility of the same-index quotient maps gives the transition identity, including for ramified extensions. The finite constant comparisons and their completed limits define Transport; their naturality and projection equations verify its six commutative squares. Apply scalar_quotient_chain_squares. Its ordinary scalar-extension functors and the chosen finiteChangeData, unrestrictedIntegralReductionFunctor and integralScalarReduction have the same prescribed sheafified tensor objects and maps. The object equalities and map formulas therefore define natural presentation isomorphisms carrying their pure tensors to finitePure, unrestrictedIntegralTensorSection and integralScalarTensorSection. Transport the supplied completed comparison and its CompletedFormula to the generic presentation, apply the generic finite theorem, and transport its output back. Whisker with the inclusion of good complexes. The forward reassociation formula sends s tensor (a tensor x) to (c_L inverse(s) * iota(a)) tensor x. Quotients insert 1 in the middle factor and reduce the outer scalar. Transitions reduce both finite scalars on the left and the single scalar on the right. Naturality of presentation transport preserves the quotient and transition squares. Restriction of scalars changes neither underlying sections nor these maps, giving exactly the displayed formulas and equalities. No projection is assumed surjective, and no coefficient map is assumed flat; the lowest level, zero complexes, and empty sites obey the same tensor identities.
